research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and OSR sources only; outcome 14-22 definitions, CSEW response/reporting and weighting, police-recorded revision/QA, comparability and governance controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSEW March 2026 provisional response rate
verified_claims: the provisional YE March 2026 CSEW response rate is 48 percent
the rate is based on the issued sample
ONS states that it is lower than historical response rates
limitations: the response rate is provisional
response rate is not the same as estimate accuracy

sources.name: Historical CSEW response comparator
verified_claims: ONS gives a pre-pandemic example response rate of 70 percent for YE March 2019
the March 2026 provisional response rate is substantially lower
the pandemic caused severe disruption to face-to-face fieldwork
limitations: the two years have different fieldwork contexts
the comparison does not by itself quantify non-response bias

sources.name: CSEW non-response adjustment
verified_claims: CSEW weighting adjusts for possible non-response bias
the aim is to make the sample reflect the general population profile
ONS says further analysis is required to understand lower-response profile variation
limitations: weighting cannot guarantee removal of all non-response bias
residual uncertainty must remain visible

sources.name: CSEW sampling-error framework
verified_claims: sample estimates differ from a full-population census result
sampling error is used to construct confidence intervals
confidence intervals express a range of plausible population values at a stated confidence level
limitations: point estimates must not be treated as exact counts
confidence intervals do not capture every non-sampling error

sources.name: CSEW Postal Address File frame
verified_claims: the face-to-face CSEW uses the Postal Address File as its sample frame
the frame covers household addresses in England and Wales
non-response is built into the sample process
limitations: the frame does not cover every non-household population
an address frame is not a parcel-risk inventory

sources.name: CSEW annual target sample
verified_claims: the target sample for the 2025 to 2026 CSEW is 31,000 interviews per year
the target supports national and police-force-area estimation
the target is a design parameter rather than the achieved sample
limitations: target interviews must not be substituted for achieved interviews
sample size does not create parcel-level observations

sources.name: CSEW police-force-area minimum design
verified_claims: the sample is designed to yield at least 585 interviews in each police force area
smaller police force areas are oversampled within the weighting design
PFA estimates remain survey estimates
limitations: 585 is a design minimum rather than an exact achieved count for every release
PFA sample sizes do not support parcel-level inference

sources.name: CSEW achieved interviews
verified_claims: 31,532 adult interviews were achieved for the 2024 to 2025 CSEW
the achieved count is reported separately from the 2025 to 2026 target
children's-survey participation is a separate component
limitations: the achieved count is edition-specific
adult interviews must not be combined with child interviews without separate bases

sources.name: CSEW unequal-selection weighting
verified_claims: raw CSEW data are weighted for unequal selection probabilities
the adjustment includes household adult counts
it also accounts for oversampling and multi-household addresses
limitations: selection weights are not risk weights
weights must remain tied to the survey design

sources.name: CSEW calibration weighting
verified_claims: calibration weighting aligns the survey to known population totals
it adjusts for differential non-response
published CSEW percentages and rates use weighted data
limitations: calibration does not make the survey a census
unweighted and weighted values must not be mixed
